sender.en: “BPI”, “BDO” or another bank, sometimes inside the bank’s real SMS thread

name.en: Fake bank text: “unusual transaction, cancel it here”

how.en: A text that looks like your bank’s usual alerts says there is an unusual transaction or a problem with your account and gives a link to “cancel” it, reactivate the account or claim a reward. Scammers use fake cell towers so the text can land in the bank’s real message thread. The link opens a copy of the bank’s website that steals your login and OTP. The BSP says banks never ask you to click a texted link to act on a transaction you did not start.

text.en: A text appears in your bank’s usual SMS thread or uses the bank’s name.
It warns of an unusual transaction, a locked account or an expiring reward.
It gives a link to cancel the transaction or update your account.
The fake site asks for your online banking login and the OTP.
BDO: An unusual transaction of PHP 18,450.00 was attempted on your account. If this was not you, cancel it immediately at [link]

A bank text with a link, even in the bank’s usual thread.
Alarm about a transaction you don’t recognise.
A site asking for your login and OTP.
Don’t tap the link. Open your bank’s app or type the bank’s address yourself to check.
Call the hotline on the back of your card if you are worried about a transaction.
If you entered your details, call your bank straight away to block online access.
Report the text to the CICC hotline 1326.
